The signature is many strings of thin pale wooden slips hung between the bamboo stems across the graves. Warm golden-hour light from the top left, long shadows of bamboo. No lit lanterns, no text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.
levels: A walled grave court with a ward-stone at each corner, and a second tower for the soul arts.
Terraced halls climb the whole hill, and the slip strings reach down to its foot.

places.name: Phục Hổ Cương
places.look: A long, low ridge on the Kinh Trập highland, shaped like a great cat crouched with its head on its paws. Its exposed rock is banded in yellow and dark grey stripes, and the grass on it is flattened into long paths.
places.lore: A tiger-kind beast holds this ridge, where the storms wake the hills. Herders say the ridge itself was a tiger that lay down to wait for the first spring thunder and never rose. When thunder rolls over the highland, the beasts on the ridge roar back, and the villages below bar their doors.
places.art_brief: A natural-site miniature with no roofline: a long low highland ridge shaped like a crouching cat, its bare rock banded in yellow and dark grey stripes, the signature; grass flattened in paths across it. Warm golden-hour light from the top left. No buildings, no text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

places.name: Vạn Xà Lâm
places.look: Deep jungle at the far end of Đan Huyệt Châu, where giant strangler figs have wrapped and swallowed older trees. Their grey roots coil over a black, still pool like nests of snakes, and real snakes lie sunning on them.
places.lore: The farthest beast lair from any town, the forest is home to snakes of every kind and the beasts that eat them. Alchemists' collectors come for venom and shed skins in the dry season, never in the wet. Locals say one snake in the forest is old enough to remember Xích Thành, and does not like fire.
places.art_brief: A natural-site miniature with no roofline: dense dark-green jungle canopy around the signature, a cluster of giant strangler figs whose pale grey roots coil like snakes over a black still pool. Steam in the air. Warm golden-hour light from the top left breaking through the canopy. No buildings, no text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

places.name: Tuyết Lang Nguyên
places.look: Open tundra on a low rise, flat and white under a wide sky. Across it runs a low ridge of frost-split grey boulders, the dark mouths of wolf dens between them and trampled snow all around.
places.lore: Snow wolves run here in packs; no sect holds the plain and no road crosses it. Frost-coast hunters say the packs answer to an old grey she-wolf never seen in daylight, and they hunt only the plain's edges in winter and leave the ridge alone.
places.art_brief: A natural site: flat pale tundra with sparse brown grass under snow, crossed by a low ridge of cracked grey boulders with small dark den openings and trampled paths in the snow around them. No buildings, no roofline. Warm golden light from the top left, long shadows from the boulders. No text, no creatures larger than specks, nothing outside the rise.

places.name: Bằng Sào Nhai
places.look: A sheer cliff of pale rock towers over the forest, and on a ledge near its top sits a nest the size of a farmhouse, woven from whole pine trunks bleached grey. Feathers longer than a man lie in the scree below. Nothing else nests within sight of it.
places.lore: A roc nests on these cliffs and hunts over the steppe and forest below. Herders drive their flocks under the trees when its shadow crosses, and Cửu Cao's riders fly their cranes wide of the cliff. Its fallen feathers are prized by fletchers and talisman (phù lục) makers.
places.art_brief: A small painted miniature of a sheer pale cliff with no roofline, a huge nest of bleached grey pine trunks on a ledge near its top, the signature element. Scree and dark forest at its base, a few long feathers in the scree. Warm golden-hour light from the top left on the cliff face. No buildings, no text, no creatures larger than specks, nothing outside the cliff.

places.name: Huyền Viên Lâm
places.look: A dense jungle below the wutong hills, where huge strangler figs rise above the canopy, their crowns knotted with the dark apes' woven sleeping platforms of branch and vine. Calls and crashing branches carry from inside, but nothing shows at the edge.
places.lore: Huyền Viên Lâm, the Dark Ape Forest, is held by no sect but by its dark apes, clever black-furred beasts that throw stones and remember faces. Herb gatherers go in only in the morning and leave fruit at the edge; those who do not, the villages say, find their way out blocked by fallen trees.
places.history: The jungle below Thê Ngô Lĩnh's wutong hills has belonged to the dark apes for as long as anyone has kept records. When Cửu Thiều Cung held the ridges, its musicians liked to say the apes sat silent at the jungle's edge to hear the palace's music. After the palace fell in the War of the Nine Shao the apes spread uphill into the empty lands for more than a century. Phượng Minh Cung, rising on those lands in the Age of Seven Seats, drove them back below the hills but never into the jungle itself. Since then the palace and the apes have kept an uneasy border: Phượng Minh's disciples hunt the edge for practice, and the apes take back what they can. No sect has tried to clear the forest, and the herb gatherers of the south prefer it that way.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a dense dark-green jungle patch with a few huge strangler fig trees rising above the canopy, their crowns knotted with dark woven platforms of branches and vine. Deep shade at the base, a thin stream at one edge. Warm golden light from the top left on the fig crowns. No text, no apes or people larger than specks, nothing outside the place's footprint.

places.name: Thương Ưng Đài
places.look: A high flat-topped stone table rises from the plateau, its cliff rim ringed with the stick nests of grey hawks and its top scoured to bare rock by the wind. The hawks circle it all day.
places.lore: Thương Ưng Đài, the Grey Hawk Terrace, is the hunting ground of the grey hawks on the high plateau near Chiết Kích Nguyên. Herders say the hawks will not fly over the poisoned plain, and that the day they do, the miasma is thinning. Young cultivators climb up to take hawk chicks for taming, and the hawks remember their faces.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a flat-topped stone mesa rising from a high plateau, its cliff rim dotted with dark stick nests, its top bare wind-scoured rock, a few tiny grey hawks circling above. Scree and sparse highland grass at the base. Warm golden light from the top left on the mesa face. No text, no people, no buildings, nothing outside the place's footprint.

places.name: Hắc Hùng Lĩnh
places.look: A forested highland ridge above the rain forest, its slopes broken by boulders. At the mouth of a dark cave stands a tilted slab of grey rock scored with deep parallel claw marks, the black bears' scratching stone.
places.lore: Black bears den in the caves of this ridge and come down to the forest's honey trees in autumn. Woodcutters of Tiêu Vũ Lâm measure their courage by how close they will walk to the scratching stone. Hunters say the freshest claw marks show how big the den's master has grown.
places.art_brief: A natural-site miniature with no roofline: a forested highland ridge with grey boulders and a dark cave mouth, before it the signature, a tilted grey rock slab gouged with deep parallel claw marks. Dense green canopy below. Warm golden-hour light from the top left, deep shadow in the cave. No buildings, no text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

places.name: Thiết Bối Cốc
places.look: A broad highland valley whose rock walls have been gnawed and scraped, so bands of raw ore gleam like polished metal along the slopes. Big grey shapes move slowly among the boulders, their backs plated like iron.
places.lore: In Thiết Bối Cốc, Iron-Back Valley, beasts with iron-plated backs feed on the ore of Ngọc Hành Sơn, grinding the veins out of the rock. Smiths prize the plates they shed, and hunters come for them; the beasts are slow and seldom angry, but a herd on the move will flatten a camp.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a broad highland valley with scraped rock walls showing gleaming metallic bands of ore, scattered boulders on the floor and a few small grey beasts with plated backs among them. Highland grass and stones at the base. Warm golden light from the top left glinting on the ore bands. No text, no people, no buildings, nothing outside the place's footprint.

places.name: Hàn Giao Chử
places.look: Out on a frozen tundra lake, a lone low islet of black rock is ringed by a coiling pressure ridge of ice that wraps around it like a serpent's body. In the thaw the ridge cracks and groans. Bones of deer and wolves lie bleached on the rock.
places.lore: Far north of Ngọc Hồ Sơn a cold flood-dragon (giao) coils around this islet, and hunters say its body is the ice ridge itself. Those who cross the frozen lake give the islet a wide berth. In hard winters its breath rises in a white column that can be seen from the shore.
places.art_brief: A small painted miniature of a small black-rock islet with no roofline in a frozen grey-white lake, encircled by a thick coiling ridge of blue-white pressure ice shaped like a serpent's body, the signature element. A few pale bones on the rock. Warm golden-hour light from the top left, blue shadows in the ice folds. No buildings, no text, no creatures larger than specks, nothing outside the islet and its ring of ice.

places.name: Băng Tê Nguyên
places.look: A frozen tundra plateau is crossed by deep trenches worn in the snow by heavy beasts. Great grey boulders stand scattered over it, scored with long gouges and polished smooth where ice rhinoceroses rub their horns.
places.lore: Ice rhinoceroses cross this plain each season, cutting the same trenches year after year. Hunters judge a herd by the fresh gouges on the rubbing stones and steer well clear. Shed horn found here is prized by the alchemists of the hills.
places.art_brief: A high, flat tundra plateau under snow, seen from above at an angle. Signature element: scattered huge grey boulders with long pale horn-gouges and polished sides, linked by deep trenches trodden through the snow. At the base: lichen patches, a frozen pool. Warm light from the top left catching the polished stone. Avoid: any roofline, text, people, beasts larger than specks, anything outside the plateau.

places.name: Vụ Báo Lâm
places.look: A steaming jungle in the island's interior, its canopy drowned in white mist most mornings. Out of the mist rises a single black rock outcrop, where the leopards bask when the sun burns through.
places.lore: Mist leopards hunt here, grey-spotted and nearly invisible in the fog; islanders say you hear one only after it has passed you. No sect holds the jungle, and Bình Thủy's ferrymen warn travellers off the inland paths.
places.art_brief: A natural site: a dense green jungle canopy half buried in soft white mist, with one dark basalt outcrop rising clear above it. No buildings, no roofline. Warm golden light from the top left on the rock and the mist tops. No text, no creatures larger than specks, nothing outside the jungle patch.

places.name: Hổ Khiếu Cương
places.look: A long bare ridge rises between the river's bends, its crest banded with dark and pale rock like a tiger's flank. The wind funnels through a notch in the crest with a low growl, and now and then a real roar answers it from the boulders below. No path crosses it.
places.lore: Herders of the lower basin say a roar on this ridge carries across all nine bends of the river, and they do not graze its slopes. A great tiger keeps its lair among the boulders, and hunters who go up for its pelt seldom come down the way they went. Tùng Đào's riders go around the ridge, not over it.
places.art_brief: A small painted miniature of a long bare highland ridge with no roofline: the crest banded in alternating dark grey and pale ochre rock like tiger stripes, the signature element, with a narrow wind notch near its middle. Tumbled boulders and dark scrub on the flanks, and one shadowed cave hollow among the boulders. Warm golden-hour light from the top left, deep shadow on the far slope. No buildings, no text, no animals larger than specks, nothing outside the ridge.

places.name: Thiên Chu Lâm
places.look: A low, steaming jungle by the bay, its canopy sagging under sheets of silver web strung from tree to tree. In the evening light the webs shine like sails across the whole wood.
places.lore: Poison spiders web this jungle so thickly that birds avoid it; no sect holds it and no road crosses it. Thiên Bảo Trai's refiners are said to buy spider silk, so a few desperate gatherers still go in with torches.
places.art_brief: A natural site: a low dense jungle canopy, deep green, draped with broad translucent silver sheets of web stretched between the treetops, catching the light. No buildings, no roofline. Warm golden light from the top left. No text, no creatures larger than specks, nothing outside the jungle patch.

places.name: Hỏa Hồ Nguyên
places.look: A flat white tundra under a low sky, broken by scattered round patches of bare, thawed brown earth. Each patch marks a fire fox den, its snow melted away by the beast's heat, and trails of melted prints run between them.
places.lore: Fire foxes run on the snow of this plain, and their dens melt round holes in the white. The cape's hunters say a fox's warmth stays in its den long after it leaves, and travellers caught by a blizzard sleep in empty dens at their own risk. Fox pelts that never freeze are the prize of a brave hunter.
places.art_brief: A flat expanse of white tundra seen from above at an angle, low lichen-covered hummocks breaking the snow. Signature element: scattered round patches of thawed brown earth, each with a dark den hole, linked by thin trails of melted footprints. At the base: snow, a frozen stream bed. Warm light from the top left, faint warm haze over the den patches. Avoid: any roofline, text, people, visible beasts larger than specks, anything outside the plain.

places.name: Tuyết Để Tuyền
places.look: A smooth snowfield lies high on the cape's mountains, white except for one blue ice cave at its foot. Steam pours from the cave mouth day and night, and the meltwater runs out warm and faintly green over the stones.
places.lore: Hot water rises under the snowfields here and carves a cave from below. Thúy Vi's alchemists climb up to bottle the water, saying it carries fire and frost together. The ice roof of the cave thins each summer, and more than one careless bather has brought it down on himself.
places.art_brief: A high mountain snowfield on a steep slope, smooth and bright. Signature element: one blue ice cave mouth at the foot of the snowfield with a thick plume of white steam pouring out, and a warm green-tinted stream running from it over grey stones. At the base: bare rock, scree, a few stunted pines below. Warm light from the top left on the snow. Avoid: any roofline, text, people, anything outside the snowfield and its stream.

places.name: Noãn Ngọc Tuyền
places.look: High in the snowy mountains, a chain of steaming pools spills down a rocky slope. The stones around them are a pale jade green and warm to the touch, and snow never settles on them.
places.lore: Băng Tâm Các holds the spring, and its disciples come here to warm meridians numbed by long ice cultivation. Mountain folk say the stones are the bones of a fire beast sleeping under Hàn Sương Châu, the same that wakes in Sương Diễm Sơn; the Pavilion neither confirms nor denies it.
places.art_brief: A natural site: a stepped chain of small steaming pools on a rocky mountain slope, rimmed with smooth pale jade-green stones that stay bare while snow covers everything around them; soft white steam drifting up. No buildings, no roofline. Warm golden light from the top left. No text, no people larger than specks, nothing outside the slope.

places.name: Hồ Tâm Thang
places.look: A small rocky islet sits in the middle of a cold mountain lake. Its hot springs have built a staircase of white and rust-orange mineral terraces down to the water, each step a steaming pool.
places.lore: Hot water at the lake's heart wells up on the islet and spills down its terraces into the cold lake. Thúy Vi disciples row out to soak and meditate there, one to a pool. Fishers say the lake never freezes within a stone's throw of the island.
places.art_brief: A small rocky islet in a dark cold mountain lake ringed by snowy slopes. Signature element: a staircase of white and rust-orange mineral terraces down the islet's side, each terrace a small steaming turquoise pool. At the base: dark lake water with a ring of open water around the islet while the lake edges are iced. Warm light from the top left on the terraces. Avoid: any roofline, text, people, anything outside the islet and its ring of open water.

places.name: Chu Sa Tuyền
places.look: In a jungle clearing, a single round hot spring boils up blood-red from the ground, steaming hard, and its overflow runs away through the trees in a bright vermilion stream. The jungle around is pale with rising steam.
places.lore: A red hot spring in the phoenix's cinnabar land, held by Phượng Minh Cung. Its water tastes of iron and stains skin pink for days. Fire cultivators come to soak after training in the vents, and herbalists scrape the red crust from the stream bed.
places.art_brief: A natural-site miniature with no roofline: a jungle clearing with the signature, one round blood-red hot spring pool, steaming, its overflow running off as a bright vermilion stream between the trees. White steam drifting into the green canopy. Warm golden-hour light from the top left. No buildings, no text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

places.name: Ngọc Nhũ Tuyền
places.look: Among grey karst pillars, a stair of milky-green pools steps down a slope, each held in a pale lip of stone the warm water has laid down over the centuries. Steam drifts between the pillars on cool mornings.
places.lore: The Jade Milk Spring rises warm among the stone pillars of Ngư Ca Xuyên's karst, its water clouded like watered jade. Lạc Hà Tông holds it but keeps no hall here: the pillars are full of caves and the beasts that den in them, so the sect sends its disciples to bathe in groups, never alone.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a cluster of tall grey karst stone pillars with a cascade of small terraced pools of milky jade-green water between them, each pool rimmed with a pale cream stone lip, thin steam rising. Dark cave mouths at the base of two pillars. Warm golden light from the top left on the pillar tops and the steam. No text, no people, no buildings, nothing outside the place's footprint.

places.name: Xích Viêm Khẩu
places.look: On a bare black cone high in Ngọc Hành Sơn, a wide red mouth glows and breathes heat, its lava cooling with a metallic sheen. A ring of carved grey warding pillars stands around the lower slope.
places.lore: Xích Viêm Khẩu, the Red Flame Mouth, is a vent of the volcano in Ngọc Hành Sơn, and the fire that comes out of it carries the mountain's metal. Thiên Xu holds it and lets no one camp inside the warding ring; its smiths and alchemists come only to draw fire for a single working and leave the same day. Miners below say the mountain grumbles before every vein war, though no one has made it prove it.
places.history: Xích Viêm Khẩu was burning before the first cultivators came to the heart, and the miners of Ngọc Hành Sơn called it the red mouth long before it had a written name. When Thiên Xu Tông took the ore mountains under its protection in the Age of First Gates, it took the vent with them. Its formation masters raised a ring of warding pillars on the lower slope to keep the vent's fire from the mines and the miners from the fire. Through the Age of Seven Seats the sect's smiths and alchemists drew fire here for workings that needed metal and flame together. After Chúc Long Sơn erupted under the ice and buried Hồ Thiên Phái in the Age of Seven Seats, the Pivot set permanent wardens at Xích Viêm, and the pillars have been kept in repair ever since. No eruption has been recorded here, and Thiên Xu means to keep it that way.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a bare black volcanic cone with a wide glowing red-orange mouth at its top, thin smoke rising, cooled lava rivulets with a dull metallic sheen down its flanks, and a ring of small carved grey stone pillars around its lower slope. Grey scree and sparse dry grass at the base. Warm golden light from the top left, the red glow strongest in the mouth. No text, no people, nothing outside the place's footprint.

places.name: Niết Hỏa Khẩu
places.look: High in the wutong hills, a fire vent opens in a slope of black ash, ringed by burned wutong stumps that have sprouted fresh green shoots from their charred trunks. Heat shimmers over the mouth, and the ash around it is warm underfoot.
places.lore: Niết Hỏa Khẩu, the Nirvana Fire Vent, lies in the hills where, the saying goes, the phoenix is reborn in fire. Phượng Minh holds it, and its fire cultivators come to temper their arts in the heat; the wutong burned by each outburst always sprouts again, which the palace takes as the vent's blessing.
places.history: The vent has breathed fire in the wutong hills since before any sect came to Thê Ngô Lĩnh. Cửu Thiều Cung's people, it is said, called it the phoenix's nest and would not go near it. After that palace fell in the War of the Nine Shao the vent burned unwatched for well over a century. Phượng Minh Cung, a sect of fire and wood, took it into its lands when it was founded and made it a place of trial for its fire disciples. Each outburst burns the wutong around the mouth and each spring the stumps sprout again, so the ring of trees has never grown tall and never died. When the palace destroyed Xích Thành Môn in the Compact years it gained the vents of Đan Huyệt Châu as well, but its elders still call Niết Hỏa their first fire.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a glowing orange fire vent in a slope of black ash high on a green hill, ringed by short charred wutong stumps each sprouting bright green shoots, heat shimmer over the mouth. Black ash fading to green grass at the base. Warm golden light from the top left, the vent's glow orange-red. No text, no people, nothing outside the place's footprint.

places.name: Hàn Diễm Khẩu
places.look: High on the ice mountains, a crack in the glacier breathes out pale blue flames that dance over the snow without melting it. The ice around the vent is glassy and scorched dark at the lip. Downwind, sulphur stains the snow yellow.
places.lore: Fire runs under the ice of Băng Tâm's land, and here it escapes as cold blue flame. Alchemists (luyện đan sư) prize its heat for furnaces that must not crack in the frost, but the ice around it is treacherous. Since Chúc Long Sơn rumbled, the nuns of Lê Hoa Am have watched this vent as closely as the mountain.
places.art_brief: A small painted miniature of a long crack in a high glacier with no roofline, pale blue flames rising from it, the signature element, the ice glassy and darkened along its lip. A yellow sulphur stain on the snow to one side. Warm golden-hour light from the top left, the blue flames glowing against it. No buildings, no text, no figures, nothing outside the vent.

places.name: Chúc Dung Khẩu
places.look: On the east coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, a low volcanic cone of black rock opens in a wide crater whose lip is shaped like an open mouth. Inside, lava glows orange, and a thin tongue of it creeps down a notch in the rim, hissing where it meets wet rock.
places.lore: Named for the fire god Chúc Dung, the vent is the most dangerous place in the land of the vermilion caves, and Phượng Minh Cung keeps watch on it. Fire cultivators say its heat teaches what no vent inland can, if they live through the lesson. Fishers along the coast read its smoke for weather.
places.art_brief: A natural-site miniature with no roofline: a low black volcanic cone near a coast, its wide crater rim shaped like an open mouth, the signature, glowing orange lava inside and a thin glowing tongue running down a notch in the rim. Grey smoke rising. Warm golden-hour light from the top left plus the lava's own glow. No buildings, no text, no figures larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

places.name: Lôi Ngô Lâm
places.look: In the lowland jungle under the storm peaks, a wood of tall wutong trees stands split and scarred by lightning, green crowns still living above trunks streaked with white burn scars and black splits. The air smells of rain and scorch, and the ground is littered with fused, glassy sand.
places.lore: Lôi Ngô Lâm, the Thunder-Struck Wutong Wood, lies under the storm peaks of Thê Ngô Lĩnh, and its trees are struck again and again yet keep growing. Phượng Minh holds it, and its instrument makers prize the struck wood for zither bodies, since a zither of thunder-struck wutong is said to answer the storm. Gatherers take only fallen wood, and never on a cloudy day.
places.history: Storms have broken on the peaks above this wood for as long as the south has records, and the tall wutong below take the lightning in their place. The court musicians of Cửu Thiều Cung, it is said, made their finest zithers from its struck wood. After Cửu Thiều fell in the War of the Nine Shao the wood went unvisited for more than a century. Phượng Minh Cung took it into its lands once it was founded, and its instrument makers came back to gather the fallen timber. When Phượng Minh went to war for the Kinh Lôi thunder vein and the Pivot left that vein with Thính Vũ, the palace's elders looked again to this wood as the south's own source of thunder. Since then the palace has guarded it more closely, and its struck timber goes only to Phượng Minh's own workshops.
places.art_brief: A natural site, no roofline: a patch of tall wutong trees in lowland jungle, their trunks split and streaked with white lightning scars and black char, crowns still green, a few fallen trunks between them, a dark storm-cloud edge at the top of the footprint. Wet dark-green undergrowth at the base. Warm golden light from the top left breaking under the cloud onto the scarred trunks. No text, no people, nothing outside the place's footprint.
